chunks: Al-Shaykh Abu 'Abd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: The garment is not washed, and the salat (prayer) is not repeated, because of what falls into the well, unless it becomes foul-smelling. If it does become foul-smelling, the garment is washed, the salat (prayer) is repeated, and the well is drained.

key_terms.الثَّوْبُ: the garment or clothing affected by the well water
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer whose validity is discussed
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being judged
key_terms.تُعَادُ: is repeated; here referring to repeating the salat (prayer)
key_terms.نُزِحَتِ: is drained out; referring to removing water from the well
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: is washed; refers here to washing the garment due to impurity
key_terms.يُنْتِنَ: to become foul-smelling; indicating change in the water's condition

ai.seo_question: If something falls into a well and changes its smell, must the garment be washed and the salat (prayer) repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water from a well when something falls into it. As long as the water does not become foul-smelling, clothes washed with it do not need to be rewashed and salat (prayer) does not need to be repeated; but if the smell changes, the garment must be washed, the salat (prayer) repeated, and the well drained.
